enhanced.fullText:
Executive Order 13465, issued in 2008 and codified at 8 CFR 274a.1, amends Executive Order 12989 to mandate E-Verify usage for federal contractors, significantly impacting higher education institutions receiving federal contracts. This regulation requires universities with federal contracts exceeding $100,000 to utilize the Department of Homeland Security's E-Verify electronic employment eligibility verification system for all employees working on covered contracts and subcontracts over $3,000.

Under 8 CFR 274a.1(b)(3), covered federal contractors must verify employment eligibility of new hires assigned to federal contracts within three business days. The regulation extends to all direct federal contractors and subcontractors, making it particularly relevant to universities engaged in federal research, construction, or service contracts. Universities must enroll in E-Verify within 30 days of contract award and maintain participation throughout the contract period, as specified in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.222-54.

Key provisions under 48 CFR 22.1803 require contractors to verify eligibility for all employees physically performing work in the United States on covered contracts, including existing employees assigned to federal contracts after the effective date. Universities must post required notices in English and Spanish as mandated by 8 CFR 274a.1(i), maintain E-Verify case documentation for three years following contract completion, and ensure subcontractors over $3,000 comply with identical requirements.

For higher education institutions, compliance encompasses faculty researchers, graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and support staff working on federal contracts. The regulation applies to Department of Education grants exceeding thresholds, NSF research awards, NIH funding, and federal construction projects. Universities must implement systematic processes to identify covered contracts and ensure timely verification of all affected personnel.

Enforcement mechanisms include contract suspension, termination, and debarment under FAR 9.406. The Department of Homeland Security may impose civil monetary penalties up to $16,000 per violation under 8 USC 1324a(e)(5). Universities face potential exclusion from federal contracting for non-compliance, making robust implementation critical. Recent amendments in 2020 clarified remote work provisions and updated penalty structures, requiring universities to verify employees regardless of work location when assigned to covered federal contracts.
enhanced.summary: Universities must use E-Verify electronic system to verify employment eligibility of workers on federal contracts over $100,000 and subcontracts over $3,000, with enrollment required within 30 days of contract award and verification completed within three business days of hire.
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No periodic reporting to federal agencies required. Universities must maintain E-Verify case documentation for three years post-contract completion, submit verification queries within three business days of employee assignment, and provide compliance certification upon contract award.
enhanced.requirements:
## Contract Coverage Requirements
- Verify all employees on federal contracts exceeding $100,000
- Include subcontracts over $3,000 in verification process
- Enroll in E-Verify within 30 days of contract award
- Maintain enrollment throughout entire contract period

## Employee Verification Obligations
- Complete E-Verify queries within three business days of hire/assignment
- Verify existing employees newly assigned to covered contracts
- Include all personnel physically performing contract work in United States
- Document verification for faculty, staff, students, and subcontractor employees

## Administrative Compliance
- Post required E-Verify notices in English and Spanish
- Maintain E-Verify case files for three years post-contract
- Include FAR clause 52.222-54 in applicable subcontracts
- Train procurement and HR staff on identification of covered contracts

## Institutional Oversight
- Designate compliance officer for E-Verify program management
- Implement systematic contract review procedures
- Coordinate between procurement, HR, and sponsored programs offices
